children: By George Glover, Mariapaula Gonzalez, and Ty Roush
Stocks fell Monday as waning peace talks between the U.S. and Iran drove oil prices and bond yields higher.

Nvidia rose 1.7%. The chip maker said it would launch the largest-ever U.S. stock buyback of $150 billion, bringing the total buyback authorization to $235 billion. The company expects to execute the remaining repurchases through fiscal 2028, which ends in January of that year.

Artificial-intelligence stocks struggled as investors opted to ditch risk assets and as OpenAI halted training of its latest models to add new safeguards. Intel declined 5.7% Sandisk fell 3.7%. Advanced Micro Devices, Corning, Dell, and Marvell also dropped.
Micron shares fell 2.6% ahead of fourth-quarter earnings on Wednesday. Revenue is expected to rise nearly fivefold, but analysts were skeptical about Micron's ability to meet memory demand.
High crude prices drove an rise in oil stocks. Chevron added o.9% and ExxonMobil gained 1.2%. APA, Baker Hughes, Devon Energy, Diamondback Energy, and Halliburton fell.

MongoDB tumbled over 18%. The company announced that President and CEO Chirantan Desai would resign effective immediately. Desai will leave the database giant to join Meta as chief enterprise platform officer.
Meta fell 4.8%, putting the stock on pace of posting back-to-back losses for the first time since mid-August.
SpaceX declined 2.2% to $145.47 as the company launched its 14th test flight for its large rocket, Starship. Separately, CLSA launched coverage of the stock with a Buy rating and a $250 price target.
Kodiak Sciences spiked 178%. The company said two experimental eye drugs met their primary goal in a late-stage study, positioning the biopharmaceutical company to get its first product to market.

Boeing fell 6.9% after The Wall Street Journal reported the plane maker identified a software glitch that could disrupt an automated landing feature. "Our engineers are working on a software update to permanently address the issue," Boeing told Barron's.
U.S.-listed shares of NIO advanced 0.3% after the Chinese electric-vehicle manufacturer said it had agreed to a strategic transaction with Geely's battery-swapping and charging businesses.

IonQ fell 2% to $44.58. Bank of America initiated coverage with a Buy rating and a $60 price target. The endorsement came after IonQ's recent acquisition of chip maker SkyWater Technology, aligning with U.S. government efforts to secure domestic quantum supply chains.

Roblox fell 9.9% to $41.86. Jefferies downgraded shares to Underperform from Hold with a $38 unchanged price target, saying the stock's 30% rally since fiscal second-quarter earnings were released represents an overly optimistic view from investors.

UiPath dropped 2.2% to $12.19. DA Davidson downgraded the stock to Underperform from Neutral and lowered its price target to $10 from $16, saying that customer pushback and confusion surrounding the software's company artificial-intelligence pricing could weigh on future growth.
Jefferies Financial and Vail Resorts report earnings after the closing bell.
